name: Beef and Mushrooms Over Rice
why: The bowl you asked for: rice, protein, vegetables, and the pickles alongside. It uses the last bag of sliced sirloin and BOTH trays of mushrooms, which came in on Aug 8 and are the things in the fridge closest to a clock. Korean home cooking calls this deopbap, which just means something on the rice. No Korean chili needed and none used, so nothing here waits on a shop. Maangchi's own opening line is that you do not need any special Korean ingredients for it.

source.name: Maangchi
source.why: Maangchi is the reference English-language source for Korean home cooking. This recipe is rated 5/5 from 281 votes and is tagged non spicy. Her sentences are kept as the instructions; everything we added is annotation.

deviations.what: Scaled x4, and 500 g of beef instead of the 454 g that x4 would give
deviations.why: 500 g is what one freezer bag holds, same rounding the bulgogi recipe already declared. x4 makes 8 of her servings; you eat it as 4 portions, which is a portioning choice and not a change to the recipe

deviations.what: Cornstarch instead of her potato starch
deviations.why: Straight 1:1 as a thickener and it is what you own. Potato starch sets slightly glossier and thins faster if boiled hard, which is why the simmer stays gentle

deviations.what: One tray of FRESH shiitake instead of her 3 dried shiitake
deviations.why: You have fresh, bought Aug 8, and they need using. This removes her several-hour soak, which exists only because hers are dried. Fresh shiitake are milder than dried, so the dish is less deeply savoury than hers. That is a real difference, not a wash
Cremini is what is in the fridge. Meaty and sliceable where enoki are stringy and stay in strands. Same job in the pan, different bite

deviations.what: Sirloin tip instead of her ribeye, plus vegetable oil
deviations.why: HER call, not ours. Her recipe note reads: If you use lean beef, you may have to add about 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil while stir-frying the beef to give it the juiciness we need. Sirloin tip is lean, so the oil is in

deviations.what: A large POT instead of her large skillet
deviations.why: x4 is about 2.3 kg of food and 4 cups of liquid. That will not fit a skillet and would slop over the side. The method does not depend on the pan being shallow

deviations.what: 600 ml of real stock plus 350 ml of water and cube, to reach her 4 cups
deviations.why: Measured 2026-08-11: 600 ml is what the carton had left after the piccata. She writes chicken broth (or beef broth or vegetable stock), so she is already flexible on it, and bulgogi.json declared this same cube swap

deviations.what: Her green chili pepper left out
deviations.why: She marks it optional in her own ingredient list

deviations.what: Cucumber pickles and pickled red onion instead of kimchi
deviations.why: She calls kimchi the one side dish you need. It is a side, not part of the dish, and nothing in the pot depends on it. You have two pickled things in the fridge that sit in exactly that slot
There is no egg in her recipe and we are not adding a step for one. Fry one on the side if you want it

deviations.what: No simmer time and no reheat time given
deviations.why: Her recipe gives neither. Rather than invent a number, both steps are governed by the doneness test instead

deviations.what: An invented browning target and an invented fond note, both REMOVED 2026-08-11
deviations.why: The doneness test said "mostly brown" and a note claimed the bits stuck to the pot were most of the flavour. Her recipe says 80 percent COOKED and never mentions fond. He cooked it and reported the beef going watery and refusing to brown, which was this annotation setting a target the dish does not have. Recorded rather than quietly deleted

Step 7 asked for a sauce that coats a spoon and holds the line, which is gravy weight. Maangchi describes just a little sticky and shiny and juicy. He cooked it exactly as written and his sauce was correct by her standard and wrong by ours. Fifth invented annotation in this one recipe, and like the other four it was an agent sentence rather than a figure from the source

time.note: The beef thaws and the rice cooks WHILE you slice, so this is about 35 min of waiting that overlaps 20 min of knife work, then 8 min in the pot

serves.proteinMath: 105 g from 500 g sirloin tip at 21 g per 100 g raw, the same figure the bulgogi recipe uses. Plus about 18 g from the rice: 2 cooker cupfuls is roughly 320 ml, or 1.35 US cups, at the 13 g per dry US cup that recipe also uses. Plus roughly 10 g from 340 g of mushrooms at about 3 g per 100 g, which is an ESTIMATE off standard values and not a label read. Plus about 3 g between the oyster sauce and the broth. Total about 136 g, divided by 4 portions, is 34 g each. It read 36 g while the rice was written as 2 US cups, which was more rice than this cooker's own cup measures out.

ingredients.display: sliced beef, the last bag from the freezer
ingredients.prep: thawed on the counter, then cut into bite-size strips
ingredients.thawText: About 20 min on the counter is all it needs: it is 2 to 3 mm slices frozen flat, not a block. You can cook this today.
ingredients.insteadOf: her ribeye, and being lean is why the vegetable oil is in

ingredients.prep: 2 cupfuls of the RICE COOKER's own cup, each filled to its top line, then rinsed until the water runs clear
caps pulled off the stems, stems thrown away, caps sliced thinly
ingredients.insteadOf: her 3 dried shiitake, which is why there is no soaking step

ingredients.prep: about three quarters of one large one, sliced thinly

ingredients.display: green onions, WHITE parts of all 4 stalks
ingredients.prep: cut into 2 inch lengths, kept in their own pile

ingredients.display: green onions, GREEN parts of those same 4 stalks, for the top
ingredients.prep: chopped, kept in their own pile
600 ml of real stock, confirmed 2026-08-11, plus 350 ml water and cube to reach 4 cups
ingredients.insteadOf: part of her 1 cup of chicken broth, made up with water and cube

ingredients.prep: HALF goes in the pot and HALF over the top at the end

steps.text: Take the bag of sliced beef out of the freezer and leave it on the counter while you do everything else. It is already sliced thin and frozen flat, so it does not need long.
steps.sourceText: 4 ounces ribeye, thinly sliced into bite size strips
steps.look: About twenty minutes on the counter is all this bag needs, because it is a thin flat sheet rather than a block. That is the figure the bulgogi recipe already established for this exact bag. There is deliberately no timer on this step: the rice and the slicing together take longer than the thaw, so by the time you reach the pot it will be ready. You are not trying to get it warm, only bendy enough to cut.
steps.warn: This bag was thawed in the fridge and refrozen once already, which is safe. It is now being thawed on the COUNTER, so it cannot go back in the freezer again. Whatever you do not cook tonight gets eaten in the next 3 to 4 days from the fridge.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, put it in the rice cooker, fill the water to the line marked 2 inside the pot, and press the lever down. Leave it alone. It clicks itself up to warm when it is done.
steps.look: USE THE COOKER'S OWN LITTLE CUP FOR THE RICE AND THE POT'S LINE FOR THE WATER. 2 cupfuls of rice, then water to the 2 line, the one with the water-drop icon. You convert nothing.The cup and the pot lines were designed as a pair, so the actual millilitres never matter. IGNORE the other scales printed on that cup: it also carries 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 40, 80, 120, 160 marks, and none of them are part of this. Fill it to the top line, twice.Recorded because it caused real confusion at the stove on 2026-08-11: this recipe first said 1 1/2 US CUPS, because the product listing claims the only included parts are an inner pot and a rice paddle, so the little cup was assumed missing. It is not missing. Introducing US cups was the single reason two incompatible scales ended up in front of a cook holding one cup. Never convert a rice cooker measurement into US cups while the cooker's own cup exists.The lid is tempered glass, so you can watch it without lifting the lid and letting the steam out.Use the fine mesh strainer, not the colander. Rice grains fall straight through a colander's holes.RINSE UNTIL CLEAR means run cold water over it, swirl it with your fingers, tip the cloudy water off, and repeat until the water coming off is see-through rather than milky. Usually three or four goes. That loose surface starch is what makes rice gluey.The cooker is the reason the rice is not a risk tonight. It is a thermostat switch, not a dial, so there is no setting to misjudge. That is what went wrong on 5 Aug and again on 8 Aug, both times on the hob.Start this before you pick up the knife. It runs unattended while you slice.
steps.warn: Capacity CONFIRMED 2026-08-11, model 2209798: 3 cupfuls maximum, which makes 6 cups of cooked rice. 2 cupfuls sits at two thirds of that and cannot boil over. Do not push it to 3 just because it fits.

steps.text: Combine the chicken broth and cornstarch in a bowl and mix well. Set aside.
steps.sourceText: Combine the chicken broth and potato starch in a bowl and mix well. Set aside.
steps.look: MEASURED 2026-08-11: 600 ml of real stock left, the rest having gone on the piccata. The dish wants 4 cups, which is 950 ml, so add 350 ml of water plus HALF a crushed Knorr cube.Why half. The box says 1 cube per 2 cups, so 350 ml of water would strictly want three quarters of a cube. Half is used instead for two reasons: cubes are scored down the middle so half is a clean split rather than a guess, and half covers about 240 ml of the 350, which puts the finished 4 cups at roughly 90% of full strength alongside 600 ml of real stock, 4 tbsp of oyster sauce and 2 tsp of kosher salt. Under-salted is fixable at the table. Over-salted is not. When two amounts are defensible, take the reversible one.Maangchi writes chicken broth (or beef broth or vegetable stock), so she is already relaxed about which broth this is.MIX WELL means stir until you cannot see white streaks or lumps sitting on the bottom. Cornstarch clumps the instant it hits hot liquid, which is why it goes into COLD broth now rather than into the pot later. This is the only thing in the recipe that thickens the sauce.
steps.warn: It settles back out while it stands. Give it another stir right before it goes in the pot, or the thickening ends up in the last spoonful instead of spread through.

steps.text: Slice everything now, before the pot goes on, because once it does the whole dish is done in eight minutes. Mushrooms sliced thinly, the carrot sliced thinly, the onion sliced thinly, and the green onions with the white parts cut into 2 inch lengths and the green parts chopped into a separate pile. Mince the garlic.
steps.sourceText: 3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked in cold water for several hours until soft, sliced thinly / 2 to 3 ounces enoki mushrooms (about 1/2 package), trim off the woody base of the stalks / 1 small carrot (about 2 ounces), cut it 2 inch long crosswise and slice thinly / 1 spicy green chili pepper (optional), chopped if using / 2 green onions, divide white and green. Cut white part into 2 inch long and chopped green part for garnish / 1 small onion (about 2 to 3 ounces), sliced thinly / 1 garlic clove, minced
steps.look: SLICED THINLY here means about the thickness of a coin, 2 to 3 mm. Everything in this dish cooks for four minutes total, so anything thicker stays raw in the middle.Do not wash the mushrooms under the tap. They drink water like a sponge and then steam instead of browning. Wipe them with a damp paper towel.Shiitake stems are woody and unpleasant to eat. Pull the cap off the stem and throw the stems away. Cremini stems are fine, just trim the dried end.THE WHITES AND GREENS GO IN AT DIFFERENT TIMES, which is why they get separate piles. The whites are the pale firm ends nearest the root and they cook with the vegetables. The dark green tops go on raw at the very end. This was the exact omission you flagged in the bulgogi cook log, so it is spelled out here.MINCE means chop as fine as you can get it, small enough that no piece is still recognisable as a slice.Your onions are SWEET onions, not yellow. They hold more sugar and water, so they collapse faster and taste sweeter than the onion she used. Nothing to change, just do not be surprised when they soften quickly.
steps.warn: Weigh the mushrooms, carrot and onion on the scale rather than guessing. The whole reason this dish is worth cooking tonight is that both mushroom trays get used, and eyeballing it is how half a tray gets left in the fridge to go off.

steps.text: Heat the large pot over high heat. Drizzle the sesame oil and the vegetable oil into the pot and add the beef, garlic, kosher salt, and ground black pepper. Stir with a wooden spoon for about 2 minutes until 80 percent of the beef is cooked.
steps.sourceText: Heat a large skillet over high heat. Drizzle 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil into the skillet and add the beef, garlic, kosher salt, and ground black pepper. Stir with a wooden spoon for about 2 minutes until 80 percent of the beef is cooked. If you use lean beef, you may have to add about 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil while stir-frying the beef to give it the juiciness we need.

heat.target: Hot before anything goes in, and hot enough that you can hear a steady crackle within a few seconds of the beef hitting it. If it goes in silently the pot is too cool.
heat.recheck: After 30 seconds. Bring it up until you can hear it.

doneness.test: Lift one piece out with the spoon and look at the cut face. She asks for 80 percent COOKED, not browned: the outside has gone from red or pink to grey-brown, with a little pink still left in the middle. That is the whole test. It finishes cooking in the sauce.

steps.look: HALF the sesame oil goes in here. The other half goes over the top at the end, which is how she splits it too.THIS DISH DOES NOT BROWN THE BEEF AND CANNOT. Her sentence says 80 percent COOKED. There is no searing step anywhere in this recipe: beef for 2 minutes, then vegetables, then broth, then a simmer. Grey-brown beef sitting in liquid is correct and is what you should expect to see. Do not chase a crust.An earlier build of this step said "mostly brown" and claimed the browned bits left in the pot were most of the flavour of the dish. Both were invented here. Maangchi never mentions fond, and he correctly reported on 2026-08-11 that the beef went watery and would not go brown. It was the annotation that was wrong, not the cooking.The vegetable oil is here on Maangchi's own instruction: her note says lean beef needs about a tablespoon of it for juiciness, and sirloin tip is lean.
steps.warn: Salt and pepper go in NOW, with the beef, and there is no more salt anywhere else in this dish except what the oyster sauce and the broth carry. That is correct and not an omission. Do not add any at the end.

steps.text: Add mushrooms, onion, carrot and the white parts of the green onions, and stir for about 2 minutes until the onion is semi-translucent.
steps.sourceText: Add mushrooms, onion, carrot, and green chili pepper (if using) and stir for about 2 minutes until the onion is semi-translucent. 2 green onions, divide white and green. Cut white part into 2 inch long and chopped green part for garnish

heat.target: Leave it where it was for the beef. The pot should still be crackling with the vegetables in it, neither silent nor spitting.
heat.recheck: After 30 seconds. Cold vegetables drop the temperature, so if the crackle stops, bring it up until it comes back.

doneness.test: Fish out one slice of onion and hold it up. SEMI-TRANSLUCENT means the thickest part has gone from solid white to slightly see-through, while the slice still holds its shape and does not flop over the spoon.

steps.look: It will look like far too much for the pot when it all goes in, and it drops by about half in two minutes. Mushrooms are mostly water and they let it go fast.Two minutes is shorter than you would cook mushrooms on their own, and that is right. They keep cooking in the sauce for the rest of the recipe.The WHITES of the green onions go in here. The chopped greens stay on the board until the very last step.
steps.warn: Her green chili pepper is marked optional in her own ingredient list and is not in this version, so there is no chilli heat in this dish at all. If you want heat, the crushed jalapeno or the sriracha go on at the table, not in the pot.

steps.text: Stir in the oyster sauce and the chicken broth and cornstarch mixture. Stir everything until it is soft and smooth. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer.
steps.sourceText: Stir in the oyster sauce and the chicken broth/potato starch mixture. Stir everything until it's soft and smooth. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer.

heat.target: Turned down until the surface is barely moving, with a bubble breaking here and there rather than all over. Not still, and not rolling.
heat.recheck: Two minutes after you turn it down. If the surface has gone completely flat and still, bring it back up until you can see the occasional bubble.

doneness.test: Her test, in her words: it should look SHINY, and a little sticky rather than like broth. Lift the spoon out and watch it drip. Drips that fall in slow fat drops and leave the spoon looking glazed is right. Drips that run off thin and fast and leave the spoon clean means give it another minute at a bubble.

steps.look: Stir the broth mixture again before it goes in. Cornstarch settles to the bottom while it stands.SOFT AND SMOOTH is her phrase and it means no lumps and no floury streaks, just an even glossy sauce.THIS SAUCE IS MEANT TO BE LIGHT, NOT GRAVY. Her own words are that she uses just a little bit of starch to make it just a little sticky, so that over the rice it looks shiny and juicy. An earlier build of this step asked for a sauce that coats the back of a spoon and holds the line where the spoon passed. That is a much thicker sauce than she describes and it was invented here, not taken from her. On 2026-08-11 he followed the recipe exactly, reported "there is a little bit of viscosity, I guess, but still watering", and was passing her test while failing ours.Cornstarch does nothing until it is near boiling, so if it looks like plain broth the pot is not hot enough yet rather than short of starch. That is also why step 8 brings it back to a full bubble.If you want it thicker than hers: 1 tbsp of cornstarch stirred smooth into 2 tbsp of COLD water, in while it bubbles, then wait 60 seconds. Repeat once if you want more. Small doses, because thickening cannot be undone.
steps.warn: This is where the pot gets full. There are 4 cups of liquid going into an already full pot, which is exactly why this is the large pot and not a skillet. Pour it in gradually rather than all at once if it looks close to the rim.

steps.text: Put the warm rice on plates, dividing it into four portions. Heat the sauce back up over high heat until it is bubbling, then spoon it over the top of the rice.
steps.sourceText: Put the warm rice on a large platter, or divide your rice into 2 portions on 2 plates. Heat up the sauce over high heat until it's bubbling and then it over top of the rice.

heat.target: Back up until bubbles are breaking across the whole surface, not just around the edge.
heat.recheck: After one minute. It comes up fast from a simmer.

doneness.test: Bubbles breaking across the whole surface of the pot rather than only at the rim.

steps.look: She is emphatic about serving this BUBBLING HOT, and the reason is mechanical rather than fussy: the sauce is what loosens the rice enough to mix, and a lukewarm thickened sauce sits on top in a lump instead of running through it.Four portions rather than her two, because this is the quadrupled batch. Rice down first, sauce over the top, and do not stir it together in the pot.

steps.text: Sprinkle with the chopped green onion, drizzle the rest of the toasted sesame oil over the top, and serve right away.
steps.sourceText: Sprinkle with the chopped green onion, drizzle 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil, and serve right away with kimchi.
steps.look: The second half of the sesame oil goes on RAW, off the heat. Toasted sesame oil is a finishing oil: cooked it goes flat and slightly bitter, drizzled on at the end it is the thing that makes the bowl smell like a restaurant.She serves this with kimchi and calls it the only side dish you need. You have no kimchi, and it costs the dish nothing. Your cucumber pickles in their own brine and the pickled red onion sit in exactly that slot, and both have been ready since Aug 9.The leafy greens are not in this dish and should not be. Spring mix wilted into a hot bowl turns bitter and collapses to nothing. Put a handful in a bowl raw with the honey Dijon or the balsamic, add pickles and pickled onion, and eat it alongside. That needs no recipe.
steps.warn: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge and reheats well, because it is a saucy dish to begin with. Microwave with a damp paper towel over the bowl. The 3 to 4 days is a hard limit and it starts tonight.

provenance.statement: Every instruction is Maangchi's own sentence, kept in her order with her times. `sourceText` on each step is the published text it came from, so any step can be diffed against the original even though the adapted tier does not require it. Amounts are scaled x4 and four ingredients are substituted, both listed in full under deviations, and that scaling and substitution is what makes this adapted rather than sourced.

sources.name: Maangchi
sources.note: Beef and mushrooms stir-fried over rice (Soegogi-beoseot-deopbap). Rated 5/5 from 281 votes, tagged non spicy. Posted 2019-04-28, last updated 2026-05-18. Fetched 2026-08-11; the site returns 403 to a plain fetch and 200 to a browser user-agent.
